paragraphs: Harrow Council fosters for children in the borough's care, and the services listed above also cover Harrow. The council's enquiries, recruitment and assessments are handled by Foster with West London, which brings eight west London councils together as one regional fostering service.

The council describes the range of fostering it needs: short-term care while plans are made for a child, long-term and permanent homes, parent and child placements, respite care (often for children with a disability or additional needs) and specialist care for children with complex needs, which is paid at a higher rate and suits carers with significant experience. Many of the children have lived through neglect, domestic abuse or parental substance misuse.

To foster for the council you need to be at least 21, with a spare bedroom for any child over two and some experience of children (you do not need to be a parent). You can rent or own your home, be single, married or in a civil partnership, and keep working if your hours are flexible. A health condition does not rule you out on its own. Council carers get a supervising social worker, 24-hour support, training, monthly support groups, free Fostering Network membership, a Blue Light Card and the backing of the Harrow Foster Carers Association. Carers approved elsewhere can transfer to Harrow under The Fostering Network's transfer protocol.
Talk to the council and to two or three of the services above before you choose, and see the Brent, Ealing and London pages if you live near the borough's edge.
